Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Mining MIIF, Forestry Commission partner to reforest Subri Forest Reserve Source : Joy Business 26 October 2026 3:14pm Audio By Carbonatix
The Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF), with support from Zijin Golden Ridge Limited, Ghana International Bank and three other financial institutions has partnered with the Forestry Commission of Ghana to rehabilitate and restore 50 acres of degraded land in the Subri River Forest Reserve as part of their corporate social responsibility on Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG).
The project is being undertaken in collaboration with the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, the Forestry Commission and the Environmental Protection Authority.
The initiative aims to restore degraded forest land, support biodiversity conservation and promote sustainable natural resource management in Ghana’s mining areas.
Under a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), the Forestry Commission will provide technical expertise and oversee the implementation of the restoration project.
Dubbed “Support of Forest Rehabilitation in Mining Regions and Promotion of Sustainability in Mining,” the project will be implemented over a two-year period and seeks to rehabilitate degraded portions of the Subri River Forest Reserve through targeted reforestation and restoration activities.
Commenting on the initiative, the Chief Executive Officer of MIIF, Justina Nelson, said the project reflects MIIF’s commitment to ensuring that the benefits of Ghana’s mineral resources are pursued alongside responsible environmental management.
“As an institution entrusted with managing Ghana’s mineral income and State interests in the mining sector, MIIF recognises that value creation must go hand in hand with environmental responsibility.
“Restoring degraded forest landscapes is not only about planting trees; it is about protecting biodiversity and ensuring that communities can continue to benefit from our natural resources for generations to come,” she said.
Mrs. Nelson added that the partnership demonstrates the importance of collaboration among government institutions and mining companies as well as local communities in addressing environmental challenges in mining regions adding:
“We believe that meaningful partnerships such as this can make a lasting difference”.
The scope of work will include site preparation, seedlings and other inputs, tree planting, monitoring and evaluation, stakeholder and community engagement, as well as Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) reporting.
The project is expected to contribute to the restoration of degraded forest ecosystems, improve biodiversity, strengthen climate resilience and promote sustainable forest management in one of Ghana’s important forest reserves.
It will also provide opportunities for local communities and other stakeholders to participate in forest restoration and conservation activities, reinforcing the importance of community involvement in protecting Ghana’s natural resources.
On his part, the Chief Executive Officer of Zijin Golden Ridge Limited, Leon Zhang added: "We approach forest restoration as a long-term responsibility, not a one-time gesture. Our own biodiversity offset programme at Atewa reflects that. This partnership with MIIF and the Forestry Commission to restore the Subri River Forest Reserve carries that same commitment and focus."
